questions.text:
Aroha and Tama are at the park. Their cat is sitting on the grass when a neighbourhood cat appears and chases it around a circular fountain.

The cat runs in a circle around the fountain.

Add a labelled arrow to show the force acting on the cat as it runs in a circle at constant speed.
questions.expectedAnswer: Arrow labelled Fc or Friction, pointing toward the centre of the circle.

questions.text:
The mass of the cat is 5.0 kg.
It is moving at 1.2 m s-1.
The centripetal force is 12 N.

Calculate the radius of the cat's path.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: 0.60 m. Merit: Calculation and explanation.

questions.text:
The cat hits a muddy patch and slides off at a tangent.

Use physics principles to explain the cat's velocity immediately after it starts moving off at a tangent.
questions.expectedAnswer: The cat moves in a straight line at constant speed of 1.2 m s-1, as the centripetal force is lost and there is no net force to change its velocity.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Velocity remains unchanged OR Fc is lost.

questions.text:
The cat slides toward Aroha. She reaches down and cushions the cat by extending her arms and gradually bringing them in. The cat takes 1.5 seconds to come to rest.

Use physics principles to explain why Aroha extended her arms rather than letting the cat stop quickly in 0.08 seconds.

Start by calculating the force in the cushioned collision (1.5 s).
questions.expectedAnswer: p = mv = 1.2 x 5.0 = 6.0 kg m s-1. Dp = Ft. 6.0 = F x 1.5. F = 4.0 N. If t = 0.08 s: F = 6.0/0.08 = 75 N. By increasing the stopping time, the force on the cat is much lower, reducing the chance of injury.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: p = 6.0 kg m s-1. Merit: F = 4.0 N AND force would be less. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
Aroha releases her 5.0 kg cat and it runs directly toward the neighbourhood cat at 1.4 m s-1. The neighbourhood cat, mass 6.0 kg, runs directly toward Aroha's cat. They collide, tangle together, and slide at 0.20 m s-1 in the direction the neighbourhood cat was originally moving.

Calculate the speed of the neighbourhood cat before the collision.
questions.expectedAnswer: Taking neighbourhood cat's direction as positive: p_before = p_after. -5.0(1.4) + 6.0(v) = 11.0(0.20). -7.0 + 6.0v = 2.2. 6.0v = 9.2. v = 1.53 m s-1. v = 1.8 m s-1.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Any relevant momentum calculated. Merit: Two momenta found. Excellence: Correct v = 1.8 m s-1.

questions.text:
Tama decides to bake scones. They measure 0.15 kg of sugar using a kitchen balance.

There are four springs in the balance. Each gets compressed 0.012 m when the sugar is added.

Add labelled arrows to show the two forces acting on the sugar.
questions.expectedAnswer: Arrows labelled correctly and same size: weight/gravity downward, spring force/support force upward.

questions.text:
Calculate the spring constant for one spring.

(Mass = 0.15 kg, compression = 0.012 m, 3 springs)
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: System k. Merit: One spring k = 40.8 N m-1.

questions.text:
When Tama brings the shopping to the front door, he has a choice of climbing the stairs or using the ramp. He finds it takes less time to go up the ramp.

Compare both routes by considering:
- work done
- force required
- power.
questions.expectedAnswer: Work done is the same (same height gained). The ramp requires less force (longer distance). Because it takes less time on the ramp, Tama has more power going up the ramp.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: ONE correct statement. Merit: TWO linked. Excellence: Complete comparison.

questions.text:
Tama uses a shelf hanging by wires. The chilli spice has mass 0.040 kg, the pepper 0.45 kg, and the uniform rack has mass 0.35 kg and is 0.50 m long.

The chilli is placed 0.20 m and the pepper 0.060 m from the left wire.

Maximum tension each wire can provide is 6.0 N.

State the conditions required for the shelf to be in equilibrium.
questions.expectedAnswer: The sum of clockwise torques equals the sum of anticlockwise torques AND the sum of upward forces equals the sum of downward forces.

questions.text: By performing suitable calculations, decide if the wires can hold the shelf with the chilli and pepper.
questions.expectedAnswer: Taking torques about wire B: Anti-clockwise torques = Fw(chilli) x 0.30 + Fw(rack) x 0.25 + Fw(pepper) x 0.44 = 0.040x9.8x0.30 + 0.35x9.8x0.25 + 0.45x9.8x0.44 = 0.1176 + 0.8575 + 1.9404 = 2.9155 Nm. This equals wire A x 0.50. FA = 2.9155/0.50 = 5.83 N. FB = total weight - FA = (0.040+0.35+0.45)x9.8 - 5.83 = 8.232 - 5.83 = 2.40 N. FA = 5.83 N exceeds 6.0 N limit, so the rack will fall.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One torque correct. Merit: One tension correct. Excellence: Full answer with conclusion.

questions.text:
Tama is going to add berries to the scones. Aroha rolls a berry along the table. The berry leaves her hand at 0.48 m s-1 and stops in front of Tama. It takes 3.0 seconds to roll along the table top.

Calculate the acceleration of the berry.

Tama now throws the berry to Aroha. The angle of the throw is 35 degrees and the initial velocity is 6 m s-1.

Calculate the vertical and horizontal components of the initial velocity.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One value found. Merit: Both correct and identified.

questions.text:
Explain the motion of the berry shown below.

Identify the type of motion.

For points A, B, and C on the trajectory, add labelled arrows to show:
- the forces acting on the berry
- the direction of the velocity of the berry.
questions.expectedAnswer: At all three points: Weight force (Fw) downward, same size. Velocity arrows tangent to the curve at each point.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Correct force or velocity arrows. Merit: Both correct at all points.

questions.text: Describe how the vertical and horizontal velocity of the berry change throughout its flight.
questions.expectedAnswer: Horizontal velocity remains constant throughout. Vertical velocity decreases on the way up, becomes zero at peak, then increases downward due to gravity.

questions.text:
The ceiling is 1.8 m above the table surface.

By calculating the maximum height and horizontal distance, determine whether the berry will reach Aroha, 2.5 m away.

(vi = 6 m s-1 at 35 degrees, vx = 4.9 m s-1, vy = 3.4 m s-1)
questions.expectedAnswer: Time to max height: 0 = 3.4 - 9.8t, t = 0.347 s. Max height: d = 3.4 x 0.347 - 0.5 x 9.8 x 0.347^2 = 0.59 m (below 1.8 m ceiling). Total time = 2 x 0.347 = 0.694 s. Horizontal distance = 4.9 x 0.694 = 3.4 m. The berry will reach Aroha (3.4 m > 2.5 m) without hitting the ceiling (0.59 m < 1.8 m).
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Time or height found. Merit: Range calculated. Excellence: Both found with conclusion.
